articles.title: Nine women in South Africa have been murdered since July. We are being told to be vigilant – but where are the warnings to men? | Nolethu Ndude
articles.description: The country has one of the highest femicide rates in the world, and women are yet again being asked to remove themselves from public life to counter it When I heard the authorities advising women in and around Kempton Park, the site of a recent spate of femicides, not to walk or run alone, to avoid isolated places and to “remain vigilant”, my immediate response was anger. Remain vigilant. How groundbreaking. Women are already vigilant. We photograph number plates before entering vehicles. We share Uber details with friends. We phone one another while walking. We watch the driver’s route and notice every unexpected turn. We avoid certain roads, certain times and certain conversations. We scan parking areas before getting out of our cars. We check the back seat. We listen for footsteps. We carry pepper spray where we can. We hold our keys in a way that makes us feel slightly less defenceless. Continue reading...

articles.title: 5 cops among 16 martyred in blast at Kohat Police Lines
articles.description: PESHAWAR: Five cops were among 16 martyred in an explosion at Kohat Police Lines, according to officials. Footage aired on television showed citizens gathered next to a building with a collapsed wall, digging through rubble and helping the injured. An initial handout from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed said the explosion occurred at a mosque at Kohat Police Lines. It added that initial reports suggested an explosive-laden vehicle was rammed into the building. In a later statement, he said that a suicide bomber detonated himself near the Special Branch building, adding that an exchange of fire was underway with Fitna al Khawarij terrorists. He confirmed that the dead included five police personnel and 11 civilians. “The operation will continue until the complete elimination of Fitna-ul-Khawarij ,” the IG was quoted as saying, adding that the police’s morale remained high. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. Separately, KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi sought a detailed report on the incident, saying the targeting of innocent citizens was “deeply regrettable and unacceptable,” as per a statement issued by his office. He directed authorities to ensure the immediate treatment for the injured. “The nation’s morale cannot be dampened by cowardly acts of terrorism,” he was quoted as saying. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast, praying for the recovery of the injured. “The entire nation stands with the security forces to eradicate terrorism,” he said in a statement. In 2010, 20 people, mostly the relatives of policemen, were killed and more than 90 injured in a remote-controlled bomb blast inside a police colony located just behind the Kohat Police Lines. This is a developing story that is being updated as the situation evolves. Initial reports in the media can sometimes be inaccurate. We will strive to ensure timeliness and accuracy by relying on credible sources, such as concerned, qualified authorities and our staff reporters.

articles.title: Police in Nigeria use tear gas on protest over miners' deaths
articles.description: Police in central Nigeria have fired tear gas at crowds protesting the deaths of 37 miners in custody on illegal mining charges. Activists dispute the official claim that a disease outbreak caused the deaths. The civil defense corps said the miners died from a suspected illness, but survivors suggest suffocation in a poorly ventilated cell. The government suspended the commandant of Niger state’s civil defense corps on Friday. The state government imposed a 12-hour curfew following attacks by protesters. Illegal mining is a significant issue in Nigeria, reportedly funding armed groups controlling the mines.
